newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat dragged off daily highs to end lower.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat dragged off daily highs to end lower.

text.p: Heavy fund sales and late pressure from outside markets dragged KCBT wheat futures off their daily highs, forcing them to close at or just above their intraday lows in fast late dealings, traders said.

Commodity brokers E. D. & F. Man International sold 5.2 million bushels May and 5.1 million July and traders said the liquidation was linked to fund activity. Traders said funds were behind Rosenthal Collins' late sale of 1.5 million May.
Wheat also drew spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans, which slipped on talk that a threatened strike at a Brazilian port had been called off.
KCBT wheat had surged higher at the midsession on short covering tied to buy stops in the May, fund buying in the July and spillover strength from CBOT corn.
The May contract touched an intraday high of $4.14, its highest level since it traded at $4.18-1/2 on Sept 12, 1996.

But KCBT wheat settled 6-1/2 cents lower to four cents higher, with May down 6-1/2 cents at $4.00. May traded in 1 15-cent range Tuesday. March lost 4-1/4 cents to close at $4.25, and July fell five cents to close at $3.76.
Benson-Quinn bought 1.3 million March, 1.5 million May and one million July, traders said.
